channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Equities: Hyperscaler stress and chip volatility – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Marco Stoeckle argues that the AI trade is at a crossroads, with ‘Mag 7’ euphoria fading and hyperscalers facing cash flow and leverage concerns. In contrast, semiconductor and memory stocks, tracked by SOX and KOSPI, saw hyperbolic gains before sharp drawdowns.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer yields curb gains ahead of FOMC – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret say broad US Dollar (USD) gains are moderating as United States (US) yields retreat and risk appetite improves after a tech-led selloff.

item.title: Euro: Choppy range view holds against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley describes EUR/USD as wary after the July European Central Bank (ECB) meeting. Foley notes that the Euro (EUR) failed to gain support despite a hawkish ECB tone, while the Dollar benefits from safe haven demand and Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations.

item.title: British Pound rises as Oil slide softens USD, Fed hike bets increase
item.description: The Pound Sterling advances by some 0.20% on Friday as Oil prices tumble, weighing on the US Dollar, while the US-Iran conflict signals a further escalation, which market participants ignored. Despite registering daily gains, the GBP/USD is poised to finish the week with losses of nearly 0.70%.

item.title: Oil: Supply risks keep prices elevated – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that Brent has retreated slightly below $100 but remains supported by renewed Middle East tensions, Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz disruptions, and Kazakhstan’s export halt. Institutional flows show high-conviction re-accumulation of energy exposure from a still-depleted base.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains slightly against US Dollar as Oil prices ease
item.description: USD/CHF trades flat on Friday as a pullback in Oil prices weighs modestly on the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields. However, the Middle East war and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations keep an underlying floor under the Greenback.

item.title: British Pound: Strong UK data fail to lift GBP against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the British Pound (GBP) is slightly higher versus the US Dollar (USD) but lagging most G10 peers.

item.title: Japanese Yen stays under pressure as resilient US economy supports the Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY edges lower on Friday, trading around 163.70, down 0.09% on the day at the time of writing, after hitting a fresh near 40-year high on Thursday.

item.title: Pakistan and Iran explore renewed US talks under China-backed diplomatic push
item.description: Pakistan and Iran are exploring a possible path toward renewed negotiations with the United States (US) as part of a new diplomatic initiative supported by China, Reuters reported, citing several sources familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS stance supports relative resilience – MUFG
item.description: Lloyd Chan at MUFG highlights that Singapore’s June inflation data stayed benign, with modest upticks in headline and core CPI. MAS is expected to keep policy unchanged in July but retain a tightening bias.

item.title: British Pound: Strong PMIs and retail rebound in focus – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes that the UK Composite PMI climbed back into expansion at 52.1 in July, led by Manufacturing strength and a Services PMI recovery to 51.8. Input cost inflation eased and business confidence hit its highest since February.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher after mixed US PMIs
item.description: AUD/USD trades higher near the 0.6990 area on Friday, recovering from an earlier pullback as the US Dollar (USD) struggles to gain clear momentum following mixed United States (US) business-activity data.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Multi-decade lows against US Dollar face BoJ risk – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Japanese Yen (JPY) is slightly firmer versus the US Dollar (USD) but still underperforming most G10 currencies. USD/JPY trades near levels last seen in 1986, with limited resistance overhead.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher yields keep upside risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny highlights that rising US and global bond yields, elevated geopolitical risks and higher energy prices are supporting the US Dollar.

item.title: Euro: Hawkish ECB and strong PMI cap downside – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that EUR/USD has recovered part of its recent slump but remains below 1.1400. A stronger-than-expected Eurozone July PMI and a hawkish hold from the ECB support the Euro, though higher Oil prices keep growth risks skewed lower.

item.title: Euro slips as strong US PMI supports Greenback
item.description: EUR/USD pares earlier gains on Friday as the widening Middle East war and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations keep the US Dollar (USD) pinned near recent highs.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles as stronger PMIs support US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4095 on Friday at the time of writing, up a modest 0.06% as the US Dollar (USD) retains a slight advantage following the release of solid US economic data, while the Canadian Dollar (CAD) remains pressured by weak domestic indicators and softer Oil prices.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Range holds against US Dollar as trade risks linger – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is little changed against the US Dollar (USD), with slightly better fundamentals as United States (US) yields ease and spreads narrow.

item.title: British Pound: BoE holds as energy risks rise – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Stefan Koopman expects the Bank of England (BoE) to keep Bank Rate at 3.75% on 30 July and unchanged through 2026, even as markets still price some chance of further tightening.

item.title: Gold steadies after sharp drop as traders weigh Fed, Middle East risks
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) steadies on Friday after falling nearly 2% the previous day, as surging Oil prices fueled expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) may need to raise interest rates amid a worsening inflation outlook.

item.title: Breaking: United States S&P Global Composite PMI improves to 53.6 in July
item.description: Business activity in the United States' (US) private sector expanded at an accelerating pace in July, with the S&P Global Composite Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) improving to 53.6 (preliminary) from 51.9 in June.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Retail sales support modest Q2 consumption – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities reports that Canadian Retail Sales rose 1.0% month-on-month in May, matching consensus but slightly below its forecast. Gains were broad-based, led by gasoline stations, autos, general merchandise and sporting goods.

item.title: South African Rand: Weakness resumes after SARB surprise – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts report USD/ZAR has broken above a multi-month descending trend line and reclaimed its 200-day moving average, suggesting renewed upside momentum. The South African Reserve Bank surprised markets by holding rates at 7.0%.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bulls retest 100-day SMA as momentum stays bullish
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) eases on Friday as traders lock in profits following a 6% jump the previous day. However, the widening Middle East war limits the downside as supply risks intensify around two major energy-shipping routes, the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ repricing may limit JPY losses against US Dollar - BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that USD/JPY is consolidating just below a multi-decade high as Japan’s private sector growth strengthens and Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks below Bank of Japan (BoJ) forecasts.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike risk rises with oil and PMIs – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that ECB President Lagarde has opened the door to a September rate hike, with sources suggesting euro area inflation must improve markedly to avoid tightening.

item.title: Euro pauses near 12-week high against Yen despite upbeat Eurozone PMI
item.description: EUR/JPY consolidates modest losses on Friday as fresh data from Japan and the Eurozone fails to generate a strong market response. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 186.30 after reaching a 12-week high of 186.67 on Thursday.

item.title: United Kingdom: Energy shock keeps risks elevated – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Stefan Koopman notes UK headline CPI fell to 2.6% in June, below the MPC’s forecast, with broad-based downside surprises and easing domestic pressures.

item.title: Economists Agree: Bank of England to stay on hold amid easing inflation outlook
item.description: The Bank of England (BoE) is expected to keep its interest rate unchanged at 3.75% at its July 30 monetary policy meeting, according to a Reuters poll of 70 economists. None of the respondents expects a change in interest rates at next week's meeting.

item.title: CEE FX: Higher rates to stabilise regional currencies – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky reports that surging Oil and gas prices triggered a sharp hawkish repricing of policy paths in Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, taking implied tightening back to stressed March–April peaks.
